title: Fit both beaters into a hand mixer, the right one in each socket
keywords: find the slot angle by turning
instruction: Fit both beaters into the hand mixer so that each is fully in and locked, then let go of everything. The mixer must stay standing on its heel rest on the table.
context: Fitting the beaters is an everyday home-baking step: people do it every time they use a hand mixer to whip cream, beat eggs or mix cake batter. KitchenAid's one hand-mixer plant built 1 million hand mixers in 2016 (Daily Advocate, 'Million mixer milestone', 16 Nov 2016, opened 2026-11-19). The maker's steps (producthelp.kitchenaid.com, 'Inserting the Beaters - Hand Mixer'): the beater with the collar goes in the larger opening; turn the flanges to the slots and push to lock; then the other beater in the smaller opening. The skill: the two beaters look alike but the collared one fits only the larger socket; the slot angle is hidden and is found by turning the beater under a light push; and the free-standing mixer slides under the locking push unless the other hand braces it. A stand mixer's beater is a different skill: one beater turned onto a bayonet pin on a heavy base, with no choice of socket, no hidden slot angle and no brace.
setup: Positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Real objects: a KitchenAid KHM512 5-speed hand mixer and its two KHM2B Turbo Beaters (part W10490648). Published figures: mixer 152 x 89 x 203 mm (6 x 3-1/2 x 8 in, AJ Madison listing for KHM512BM), 0.9 kg (2.0 lb, The Brick listing for KHM512IC); beaters stainless steel, about 38 mm across and 178 mm long (1-1/2 x 7 in, heima.com parts page and an amazon.ca parts supplier), 1/4 in stem (Speedy Appliance Parts, W10490648). The socket face is a round plastic cap with two round holes, about 38 mm apart (read from the photo in iFixit's guide 'KitchenAid KHM512ER Beater Rings Replacement'). (1) Hand mixer as simulated: white ABS, 0.9 kg, standing upright on its rubber heel rest. Housing 70 x 90 x 190 mm above a 125 x 80 x 10 mm heel rest; handle loop behind the housing: a 25 x 25 mm bar 135 mm tall joined by two 30 mm struts. The underside (socket face) faces the robot's right arm (-y), the handle faces the left arm. Two sockets 38 mm apart, centres 65 mm above the table: the larger opening 14.5 mm square, the smaller 11.8 mm square, in a 4 mm face plate. Inside each: a brass drive spindle (13 mm across, four 3 mm slots, from 4 to 19 mm deep) geared to the motor so it holds its angle; then a 7.2 mm bore to 38 mm deep with a spring clip (4 mm steel ball at 30 mm depth, sprung into the bore). Start: footprint centre at x 300 mm, y +20 mm, each trial moved up to +/-30 mm in x and y and turned up to +/-20 deg; each spindle at a random angle (0-90 deg). (2) Collared beater as simulated: stainless steel wire beater, 60 g, 190 mm long: 6 mm stem, 13 mm collar 32-36 mm from the tip, four fins 10 mm across, 2 mm thick, 24-32 mm from the tip (between collar and tip), a 4 mm wide groove 4.5-8.5 mm from the rounded tip; cage of four wire blades 38 mm across and 70 mm long. (3) Plain beater: the same with a 10 mm shoulder in place of the collar, 55 g. Both lie flat on two blades in front of the mixer, stems pointing +y toward the socket face, tips at y -65 mm (+/-12 mm), one at x 185 mm, the other at x 115 mm (+/-8 mm), each turned up to +/-12 deg; which beater lies in which place is random. Simulated sizes that are estimates, and how they differ from the published ones, are listed in the fidelity note and the README. The screenshot shows seed 0. Real trial: the seed's layout is drawn on paper under the table's clear mat; spindle angles are set by hand to the README's list (paint dot on each spindle).
scoring: Scored at the end of the run. Per beater (0.4 each): 0.1 if its stem is in a socket (tip at least 6 mm past the socket face, on the socket axis within 1.5 mm and 6 deg); +0.1 if the fins are in the slots (tip at least 30 mm deep; with the fins off the slots the tip stops at 28 mm); +0.2 if clipped (tip within 1.5 mm of full depth, 36 mm, and the clip ball back in the groove). The collared beater counts only in the larger socket; the plain one in either (the maker: a beater without a collar fits either opening). +0.2 if at least one stem is in a socket and the mixer stands on its heel rest (tilt at most 5 deg) with its footprint centre within 5 mm of where it started. So the untouched scene scores 0. The trial scores 0 unless both grippers end at least 20 mm from the mixer and both beaters. Real trial: the thresholds come from a one-time calibration of each mixer and beater pair, not from estimated sizes. Before the trials the operator, with a steel ruler, for each beater in its own socket: reads the beater's length L; pushes it fully home by hand until it clicks and reads the length showing from the socket face to the end of the cage (full-seat reading F); then turns it so the stem's tabs are off the spindle slots, pushes until it stops and reads again (blocked reading B). In a trial, with the same ruler: in a socket = the stem's tip is inside the hole (showing length L - 6 mm or less); tabs in the slots = showing length shorter than B - 2 mm; clipped = showing length within 2 mm of F and the beater stays in when the mixer is lifted 10 cm by its handle and held 3 s. Expected values from the published figures (the operator's readings replace them): L 178 mm (7 in, published); F 137 mm for the collared beater (178 mm less 41 mm, the collar's distance from the tip in the Speedy Appliance Parts W10490648 grid photo); B is longer than F by the slot depth, which is not published. Mixer: tape measure from the marked start; it stands on its heel rest. A photo shows both grippers clear.
reset_notes: Press the mixer's ejector (in the real trial) or pull each beater straight out, lay both beaters flat beside the mixer as the seed's layout gives, and turn each drive spindle to the seed's angle by hand (paint dot on the spindle, angle from the list in the README).
fidelity: Rigid PhysX bodies; all by contact, joints and springs, no attach rule. Clip: one sprung 4 mm ball (15 N preload, estimated) into a stem groove; the KHM512 holds the beater by a spring ring whose metal tabs click over the stem's tabs (iFixit), the same kind of latch. Estimates that differ from published: stem 6 mm (1/4 in), four fins (real: two tabs), beater 190 mm (7 in), 55-60 g, square holes (real: round). Spacing and cage 38 mm match photo and supplier figures. Blades do not collide.
scores: Dream-1, seed 0: 0.0 (1,200 steps). Scripted demo, reads object poses from the simulator: 1.0 on seeds 0, 1 and 2 (871 to 872 steps). Wrong outcomes on seed 0: nothing done 0.0; fixed plan 0.0; no brace 0.8; beaters swapped 0.6.
